answer: A port scanning attack involves an adversary using various techniques to determine the state of the ports on a remote target. Each service or application that operates over TCP or UDP networking will have specific ports open for communication. The attacker typically requires logical access to the target's network and may use network mapping or scanning tools, as well as packet injection tools, to perform the scan. In some cases, network sniffing may be necessary to capture responses from the target [Source 1][Source 3].

# Port Scanning

## Metadata

- Attack key: `port_scanning`
- Category: `reconnaissance`
- Origin: `clean`
- Document status: `generated_from_authoritative_sources`
- CAPEC ID: `CAPEC-300`
- ATT&CK ID: `T1046`

## Attack description

An adversary uses a combination of techniques to determine the state of the ports on a remote target. Any service or application available for TCP or UDP networking will have a port open for communications over the network.

## Prerequisites

These scans may also include more broad attempts to [Gather Victim Host Information](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1592) that can be used to identify more commonly known, exploitable vulnerabilities. ## Prerequisites

The adversary requires logical access to the target's network in order to carry out this type of attack.

## Required resources

The adversary requires a network mapping/scanning tool, or must conduct socket programming on the command line. Packet injection tools are also useful for this purpose. Depending upon the method used it may be necessary to sniff the network in order to see the response.

## Consequences
